chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

High prices and drought struck the people of Medina, to the extent that the affluent man would mix wheat with barley and eat it, and buy only part of the food (required). There was good quality food with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) which he had bought at the beginning of the year. So he said to one of his adherents: 'Buy some barley for us so I can mix it with this food, or sell it, for we dislike that we should eat good quality food while the people eat the perished (food).'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq demonstrate social responsibility during times of economic hardship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructed his followers to mix their high-quality food with lower-quality grain or sell their surplus during times of scarcity and high prices. This was done to avoid the ethical issue of the wealthy eating well while the general populace suffered from poor quality or scarce food, demonstrating social solidarity and moderation in consumption. This practice, known as *khalṭ*, reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere poverty, but as a conscious choice to share in the community's hardship, ensuring that the elite do not insulate themselves from the broader societal experience of scarcity.
